South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 77 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 05/10/25 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management and evaluation of persistent lower extremity edema.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit concerning his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and ongoing issues with bilateral lower extremity edema. He reports that his respiratory symptoms have remained stable, with continued use of his albuterol inhaler on an as-needed basis, averaging about once every other day. He has maintained his regimen of fluticasone/salmeterol and expresses satisfaction with its efficacy, stating he feels capable of managing his baseline symptoms adequately. He has not experienced any exacerbations since the last visit.
However, Mr. Fairfax notes that while the overall quality of his sleep has not changed, he has been experiencing intermittent episodes of mild wheezing, particularly in the mornings when the weather is cool. He denies experiencing nocturnal dyspnea, significant cough, or hemoptysis.
Regarding his lower extremity edema, he expresses concern that the swelling has not completely resolved despite adherence to the furosemide regimen. The edema remains at 1+ pitting, and while he has adhered to dietary sodium restrictions, he reports occasional noncompliance with leg elevation due to discomfort. He denies any associated symptoms such as pain, erythema, or warmth in the legs, and he has not experienced any chest pain or shortness of breath.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + stable energy levels, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - - cough, - sputum production, + mild wheezing, - dyspnea on exertion, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily 4. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain 5. Furosemide 20 mg daily
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 74, BP 126/74, RR 18, O2 sat 95% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 7.9, Hgb 13.5, Hct 39.8, Plt 220 2. BMP: Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 100, CO2 28, BUN 14, Cr 0.9, Glucose 92 3. BNP: 400 (slight increase from previous visit) 4. CXR: Stable hyperinflation of lungs, no acute changes.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Continue current inhaler regimen. Patient education reinforced regarding recognizing early signs of exacerbation and the importance of adherence to inhaler use. Schedule follow-up in 2 months or sooner if symptoms worsen. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains well-controlled. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: Given the persistence of edema, consider increasing furosemide to 40 mg daily. Instruct the patient to monitor weight daily and adhere strictly to sodium intake recommendations. Reassess in 1 month. 4. Follow up with pulmonary medicine for ongoing management.
Patient education emphasized regarding fluid management strategies, the importance of maintaining a heart-healthy diet, and adherence to medication regimens.
